messages.author: b7c2064c737945ab
messages.subject: cache=TRUE conflicts with foreach
parts:
When set cache=TRUE, I find knitr behaves strangely. For example,
I use foreach for parallel computing. foreach will export related
objects to different workers automatically. However, this behavior
changes when set cache=TRUE.

Any idea about this?

Thanks very much!

The following script can be run through knitr to reproduce the
problem:


-------------------------------------------------------------------------
<<>>=
require(doSNOW)
library(foreach)
registerDoSNOW(makeCluster(4, type = "SOCK"))
getDoParWorkers()
@

When cache=TRUE, function defined in the same chunk can be
successfully exported automatically by foreach:

<<test, cache=TRUE>>=
set.seed(100)
m <- matrix(rnorm(400), 200, 2)
myMean <- function(x) mean(x)

time <- system.time(res <- foreach(i=1:nrow(m), .combine='c') %dopar%
{
myMean(m[i,])
})
res[1:3]
apply(m[1:3, ], 1, mean)
@

However, if the user defined function is not within the same chunk,
foreach cannot export this function:
<<test2, cache=TRUE>>=
time <- system.time(res2 <- foreach(i=1:nrow(m), .combine='c') %dopar%
{
myMean(m[i,])
})
res2[1:3]
apply(m[1:3, ], 1, mean)
@

Mannually exporting the user defined function also fails:
<<test3, cache=TRUE>>=
time <- system.time(res3 <-
foreach(i=1:nrow(m), .combine='c', .export='myMean') %dopar% {
myMean(m[i,])
})
res3[1:3]
apply(m[1:3, ], 1, mean)
@

If cache=FALSE, everything is fine:

<<test4>>=
time <- system.time(res4 <- foreach(i=1:nrow(m), .combine='c') %dopar%
{
myMean(m[i,])
})
res4[1:3]
apply(m[1:3, ], 1, mean)
@

messages.author: 30b406a9189eeb25
messages.subject: Re: [knitr] cache=TRUE conflicts with foreach
parts:
Hi Nicky,

Manually exporting works fine.  Looks like your manual export forgot to export the 'm' variable.  
In explicitly created parallel environments, I find I usually need to keep the chunk(s) that create the parallel environment as cache=FALSE.  

I was surprised that the non-cached example in your forth chunk worked at all -- I'm more used to `snow` than `foreach`, surprised that foreach works as it does without manual export.  Not 100% sure what's going on there.  

-Carl

messages.author: cc1ef8c8158d6b73
messages.subject: Re: [knitr] Re: cache=TRUE conflicts with foreach
parts:
I'm not sure if this is knitr's fault. I would ask the foreach authors
to reconsider their decision on the .export argument. This surprised
me:

require(doSNOW)
library(foreach)
registerDoSNOW(makeCluster(4, type = "SOCK"))
getDoParWorkers()

m <- matrix(rnorm(400), 200, 2)
myMean <- function(x) mean(x)
# works, of course

res <- foreach(i=1:nrow(m), .combine='c') %dopar% {
myMean(m[i,])
}

# does not work in a new environment
eval(quote(res <- foreach(i=1:nrow(m), .combine='c') %dopar% {
myMean(m[i,])
}), envir = new.env())

I do not understand why foreach does not recognize objects like
'myMean' in the global environment. The global environment is the top
environment in R, and all other environments should be able to use the
objects there.

Regards,
Yihui
--

messages.subject: Re: cache=TRUE conflicts with foreach
parts:
Adding an environment to foreach is smart!
Yihui's code modified as below actually works, even setting cache=TRUE

<<test2-InGlobalEnvironment, cache=TRUE>>=
eval(quote(time <- system.time(res2 <-

foreach(i=1:nrow(m), .combine='c') %dopar%
{
myMean(m[i,])
})), envir = .GlobalEnv)

res2[1:3]
apply(m[1:3, ], 1, mean)
@

The original script is also updated with this partial solution at:
https://github.com/nickytong/catchAndforeach

Still, it would be nice if knitr can let foreach do what it does
outside knitr. Otherwise, I have to add the environment setting
whenever I use knitr and delete it if I'm out of knitr...

Thanks!

Nicky

messages.author: b7c2064c737945ab
messages.subject: Re: cache=TRUE conflicts with foreach
parts:
Hello Yihui,

I'm not sure if I get your point. My understanding is that foreach
works fine by itself before interacting with knitr. For example, when
I extract the R code and run it in R console (not through knit()), I
get what I need. When I use the same code but in knitr environment,
foreach cannot automatically export objects as it is designed. I guess
this is because knitr somehow modify the local environment where
foreach chunk is executed. If we explicitely gives the global
environment to foreach, it works fine as in：

eval(quote(time <- system.time(res2 <-
foreach(i=1:nrow(m), .combine='c') %dopar%
{
  myMean(m[i,])
})), envir = .GlobalEnv)

Note I set envir = .GlobalEnv, which means everything is accessible by
foreach.

In your example:
eval(quote(res <- foreach(i=1:nrow(m), .combine='c') %dopar% {
 myMean(m[i,])
}), envir = new.env())

Setting envir = new.env() gives a nude environment to foreach. Of
course, myMean function is not defined in this empty environment. As a
result, foreach cannot find myMean() and fails to export it.
Why would you expect foreach to work in this case?

I still don't quite get what to report the foreach author, though...

Thanks for your time and efforts and the wonderful tool!

Best,

Nicky

messages.author: cc1ef8c8158d6b73
messages.subject: Re: [knitr] Re: cache=TRUE conflicts with foreach
parts:
My point is, new.env() has a parent frame by default which is
.Globalenv in this case, so why should not foreach be able to find
myMean? Inheriting objects from parent frames is a very common
behavior in R, e.g.

x = 5
eval(quote(x + 1), envir = new.env())

This works fine, but foreach works differently. It probably needs to
change its way to search for objects, but since it has a '.export'
argument, they may argue they do not have to do it.

Regards,
Yihui
--
